source.title: Open Problems for the 2025 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop

accepted.question_text: Let G be a strongly 2-connected digraph together with a real weight w(e) on each edge such that for every directed cycle of G, the sum of the edge-weights on that cycle equals 1. Determine whether every such weightable digraph must be planar. A stronger structural question from the source asks whether every strongly 2-connected, weakly 3-connected, weightable digraph arises from a planar drawing equipped with a vector-field construction of the kind described there.

evidence.quote: Suppose that G is a strongly 2-connected digraph and for every edge e, w(e) is some real number, such that for every directed cycle, the sum of w(e) over the edges of the cycle equals 1. Does G have to come from a planar drawing in this way? In particular, does G have to be planar?

So here is the current set of conjectures: (1) If G is strongly 2-connected and weightable, then G is planar; (2) If G is strongly 2-connected, weakly 3-connected, and weightable, then there is a drawing of G in the plane and vector field of the form described above so that G is given by the above construction.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the digraphs in which every directed cycle has length exactly 4. More generally, determine what happens when every directed cycle is required to have one fixed prime length.

evidence.quote: What are the digraphs in which every directed cycle has length four? I know the answer if they all have length three ... but I can’t do length four. What if they all have length some nice big prime number, is that easier?

accepted.question_text: For a graph G, let tree-tw(G) denote the minimum k such that G has a tree-decomposition whose every bag induces a subgraph of treewidth at most k. Determine the maximum possible value of tree-tw(G) for K_t-minor-free graphs G, and in particular decide whether every K_t-minor-free graph satisfies tree-tw(G) = O(t^2).

evidence.quote: In particular, what is the maximum of tree-tw(G) for a Kt-minor-free graph G? Liu–Norin–Wood gave a lower bound of Ω(t2), and asked whether Kt-minor-free graphs G have tree-tw(G) ∈ O(t2)?

accepted.question_text: A hereditary graph class G is called (tw,had)-bounded if there is a function f such that tw(H) ≤ f(had(H)) for every graph H in the class, and it is linearly (tw,had)-bounded if tw(H) ≤ c·had(H) for some constant c and every H in the class. Determine whether every hereditary graph class that is (tw,had)-bounded is automatically linearly (tw,had)-bounded.

evidence.quote: Campbell–Davies–Distel–Frederickson–Gollin–Hendrey–Hickingbotham–Wiederrecht–Wood–Yepremyan asked for what classes of graphs is a reverse inequality true?
Campbell et al. conjectured that every (tw,had)-bounded hereditary graph class is linearly (tw,had)-bounded.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the Grid Minor Theorem can be strengthened to have polynomial dependence on t and linear dependence on k, namely: does every graph of treewidth at least t^c k contain either a K_t minor or a k × k grid minor for some absolute constant c?

evidence.quote: Does the Grid Minor Theorem hold with polynomial dependence on t and linear dependence on k? That is, does every graph with treewidth at least t^ck have a Kt minor or a k × k grid minor?

accepted.question_text: Let S and S′ be graph classes defined by finitely many forbidden subgraphs, induced subgraphs, minors, induced minors, topological minors, or induced topological minors. Determine whether inclusion S ⊆ S′ is decidable in the general case. Related open directions in the source ask whether one can decide the existence of added induced paths with constrained neighborhoods that avoid a finite forbidden family, and whether one can decide the existence of an F-free Hamiltonian graph containing a prescribed graph H.

evidence.quote: Is it decidable to determine if S ⊆ S′?
We suspect the general case is undecidable.
Similar methods can be used to prove the following problem is undecidable. Let H be a graph and F a finite set of graphs. Is there an F-free Hamiltonian graph containing H?

accepted.question_text: For every tournament H, determine how large an acyclic induced subdigraph must exist in an H-free digraph G, equivalently how small the dichromatic number of H-free digraphs must be. In particular, improve the known lower bound in the cyclic-triangle-free case H = C_3, and determine whether the current bound on the dichromatic number of C_3-free digraphs in terms of the stability number can be strengthened from α(G)^{O(α(G))} to a singly exponential bound or better.

evidence.quote: For every tournament H, there exists c > 0 such that every H-free digraph G has an acyclic induced subdigraph with at least |G|^c vertices.
given the recent work on the EH conjecture, can a bound of 2^c √(log |G| log log|G|) be proven in this case?
Can a singly exponential bound be done in this direction?

accepted.question_text: Determine clustered-colouring bounds under girth assumptions for sparse graph classes: (1) whether graphs of sufficiently large girth and bounded treewidth are 2-colourable with bounded clustering depending on the treewidth, and likewise for bounded pathwidth; (2) whether K_t-minor-free graphs of sufficiently large girth are 3-colourable with bounded clustering depending on t; and (3) whether K_t-minor-free graphs of sufficiently large girth are 2-colourable with bounded clustering depending on t.

evidence.quote: Are graphs with girth at least some absolute constant and with bounded treewidth 2-colourable with bounded clustering?
Are Kt-minor-free graphs with girth at least some absolute constant 3-colourable with bounded clustering (depending on t).
Are Kt-minor-free graphs with girth at least some absolute constant 2-colourable with bounded clustering (depending on t)?

accepted.question_text: Let f_3(n) be the minimum clustering needed to 3-colour every n-vertex planar graph. Determine the correct asymptotic order of f_3(n). The source also highlights a related island problem: determine the least function g(n) such that every n-vertex planar graph has a vertex set S of size at most g(n) where each vertex of S has at most two neighbors outside S, since a greedy argument gives f_3(n) ≤ g(n).

evidence.quote: Linial et al. showed that f2(n) = Θ(n2/3) and Ω(n1/3) ⩽ f3(n) ⩽ O(n1/2). Determining f3(n) is wide open.

what is the least function g(n) such that every n-vertex planar graph G has a set S of at most g(n) vertices, such that every vertex in S has at most two neighbours in V (G) \ S? A greedy colouring algorithm shows that f3(n) ⩽ g(n).

accepted.question_text: A sun is obtained from a cycle by attaching one pendant edge at each cycle vertex. Determine whether the class of graphs containing no sun as an induced subgraph is χ-bounded. In particular, settle the triangle-free case, equivalently whether graphs with no triangle and no induced sun of length at least 4 have bounded chromatic number.

evidence.quote: Are sun-free graphs χ-bounded?
The triangle-free case is of interest and can be rephrased as: is there an upper bound on the chromatic number of graphs with no triangle and no sun of length at least 4 (as induced subgraphs)?

accepted.question_text: For the triangle-free case of the El-Zahar–Erdős conjecture, determine how large the chromatic number threshold d(2,t) must be to force two disjoint anticomplete vertex sets A and B with χ(G[A]) and χ(G[B]) at least t. The source specifically asks about an ultra-strong linear bound d(2,t) = O(t), but also records evidence that this stronger form is false, so the remaining problem is to understand the correct growth rate in the triangle-free setting.

evidence.quote: In particular this remains open when w = 2, that is when G is triangle-free.

Is there a counterexample to the following ultra-strong strengthening? There exists C > 0 such that for every integer t ≥ 1, every triangle-free graph G with χ(G) ≥ Ct contains two disjoint anticomplete vertex subsets A and B with χ(G[A]), χ(G[B]) ≥ t.
That’s great! Thanks for the explanation! So that means the statement I proposed is very false in fact, beyond what I had hoped for.

accepted.question_text: Prove Hadwiger’s conjecture for the following graph classes singled out in the source: graphs whose every induced subgraph H satisfies χ(H) − ω(H) ≤ 2; (P_5, C_5)-free graphs; (P_5, complement of P_5)-free graphs; and ISK_4-free graphs, meaning graphs with no induced subdivision of K_4. The source also asks whether the class of (P_5, complement of P_5)-free graphs satisfies a linear Hadwiger bound and points to complements of line graphs of triangle-free graphs as another potentially interesting special case.

evidence.quote: Prove Hadwiger’s conjecture for 1. Graphs all of whose induced subgraphs H satisfy χ(H) − ω(H) ≤ 2 2. (P5, C5)-free graphs 3. (P5, P c5)-free graphs 4. ISK 4-free graphs
From Tung: Is it known whether {P5, P5}-free graphs satisfy linear Hadwiger?

accepted.question_text: Let two graphs on the same vertex set be at distance at most d if one is a pivot-minor of a graph obtained from the other by adding at most d vertices. Give a qualitative characterization of the pivot-minor-closed classes consisting of graphs at bounded distance from bipartite graphs. In particular, determine whether excluding both K_n and the direct sum of n triangles as pivot-minors forces distance at most f(n) from a bipartite graph.

evidence.quote: Can we find a qualitative characterization for this class? Is it enough to exclude Kn and the direct sum of n triangles? That is, if G is a graph that contains neither Kn nor the direct-sum of n triangles as a pivot-minor, is G at distance at most f(n) from a bipartite graph?

accepted.question_text: Determine the sharp regularity thresholds forcing bounded chromatic number in dense H-free graphs: specifically, whether every K_5-free 0.7n-regular graph on n vertices has bounded chromatic number without the additional +εn slack, and whether every triangle-free n/4-regular graph has bounded chromatic number.

evidence.quote: The threshold 0.7 is best possible, but can we drop the εn term? Also, do n/4-regular triangle-free graphs have bounded χ?

accepted.question_text: Improve the known domination bounds for tournaments with bounded fractional chromatic number or bounded fractional VC-dimension. The source asks whether the current domination-number bound O(k^k) for tournaments of fractional chromatic number k can be improved to poly(k), what the best possible bound f(k) is when every out-neighborhood has chromatic number at most k, whether bounded fractional VC-dimension is useful more broadly, and whether T_k-free or S_k-free tournaments have bounded fractional VC-dimension.
accepted.context_brief: Domination and fractional VC-dimension in tournaments

evidence.quote: Can the bound be improved to poly(k)?
What is the best bound for f?
Is it useful for anything?
Is it true that Tk-free tournaments have bounded fractional VC-dimension?

accepted.question_text: Let H be a fixed graph and K a positive integer. Determine whether there exist functions c and d such that every graph with no K-fat H-minor is (c(H), d(H,K))-weak diameter colourable, meaning it admits a c(H)-colouring in which each monochromatic component has weak diameter at most d(H,K).

evidence.quote: Conjecture: There exist functions c, d such that every graph G with no K-fat H-minor is (c(H), d(H, K))-weak diameter colourable.

accepted.question_text: Suppose φ is an (L,C)-quasi-isometry from a graph G to a graph H of treewidth at most k. Determine whether one can adjust edge weights so that the same map becomes a quasi-isometry with multiplicative constant 1. The source records a strong conjecture weighting only H and a weaker conjecture allowing weights on both G and H while requiring the zero-weight components in G to have bounded weak diameter.

evidence.quote: Conjecture: For all k, L, C ∈ N there exists C′ ∈ N such that if ϕ is an (L, C)-quasi-isometry from a graph G to a graph H where tw(H) ≤ k, then there is a function w : E(H) → N0 such that the same function ϕ is a (1, C′)-quasi-isometry from G to the weighted graph (H, w).

Conjecture: For all k, L, C ∈ N there exists d, C′ ∈ N such that ... there are functions wH : E(H) → N0 and wG : E(G) → N0 ... and the same function ϕ is a (1, C′)-quasi-isometry from the weighted graph (G, wG) to the weighted graph (H, wH).

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the class of k-gap planar graphs has bounded asymptotic dimension. A warm-up problem highlighted in the source is to determine the weak-diameter chromatic number of the class of k-gap planar graphs.

evidence.quote: Does this class of graphs have bounded asymptotic dimension?
A warm-up question to this problem is to first determine the weak-diameter chromatic number for the class of k-gap-planar graphs.

accepted.question_text: For the sequence of Burling graphs, define B(G) as the largest i such that G contains B_i as an induced subgraph. Determine whether there is a polynomial-time algorithm to compute B(G), at least for Burling graphs, and whether there is a polynomial-time approximation algorithm that outputs s with s ≤ B(G) ≤ f(s) for some increasing function f.

evidence.quote: Is there a polynomial time algorithm for determining B(G)? What if G is a Burling graph?

Is there a polynomial time approximation algorithm? To be more precise, is there some increasing function f and a polynomial time algorithm that outputs some s so that s ≤ B(G) ≤ f(s). What if G is a Burling graph?

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) be the largest integer such that every connected vertex-transitive digraph on n vertices contains a directed cycle of length at least f(n). Prove a nontrivial lower bound on f(n), in particular decide whether there exists ε > 0 with f(n) ≥ n^ε. The source notes that these lower-bound questions have since received positive answers.
accepted.context_brief: Long directed cycles in vertex-transitive digraphs

evidence.quote: Can you prove a non-trivial lower bound on f(n)? In particular, is there ε > 0 such that f(n) ≥ n^ε?
We (Bućic, Hendrey, Mohar, Steiner, Yepremyan) now have positive answers to these questions.

accepted.question_text: Let og(n) be the minimum odd-girth threshold that forces every n-vertex graph to have chromatic number at most 8. Determine the best asymptotic bound for og(n). Also determine whether one can replace the target bound 8 by 3 while still keeping og(n) = o(n). The source records progress showing og(n) = O(n^{1/7}) and that the second question has a positive answer with O(√n), but the optimal behavior remains open.
accepted.context_brief: Odd-girth thresholds for bounded chromatic number

evidence.quote: What is the best bound for og(n)?
Can we replace 8 by 3 and still get o(n)?
It implies that og(n) = O(n1/7). Also it shows that the answer to the second question is positive, one can get even O(√n) for 3 instead of 8.

accepted.question_text: Design a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether an input graph contains induced cycles of three different lengths. A harder variant asks for a polynomial-time algorithm deciding whether the graph contains holes of three different lengths, where a hole is an induced cycle of length at least 4.

evidence.quote: Problem 1: Decide in polytime if an input graph contains induced cycles of three different lengths.
Problem 2, possibly more difficult: Decide in polytime if an input graph contains holes of three different lengths, where a hole is an induced cycle of length at least 4.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every triangle-free graph with independence number α has at most 2^{O(α)} maximum independent sets.
accepted.context_brief: Maximum independent sets in triangle-free graphs

evidence.quote: Is it true that in a triangle-free graph of independence number α there are at most 2O(α) maximum independent sets?

accepted.question_text: Given a properly edge-coloured n-vertex graph G of average degree at least on the order of log n, determine whether one can always find a vertex subset U and a partition of the colours into C_1 and C_2 such that the induced subgraph G[U] is connected using only colours from C_1 and also connected using only colours from C_2.
accepted.context_brief: Discrete X-ray reconstruction via coloured graphs

evidence.quote: Given a properly edge coloured n-vertex graph G with average degree d ⩾ O(log n) show that one can find a subset of vertices U and a partition of the colours into two sets C1, C2 such that G[U] is connected using only edges of colors in C1 and only using edges of colors in C2.

accepted.question_text: Fix an integer d > 1. Prove that in every connected d-regular graph on n vertices, the multiplicity of the second-largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix is o(n / log log n).

evidence.quote: Let d > 1 be a fixed integer. Prove that in any d-regular connected graph on n vertices the multiplicity of the second largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix is o(n/ log logn).

accepted.question_text: Characterize the hereditary graph classes C for which there exists a function f satisfying χ(G) ≤ f(χ_f(G)) for every graph G in C, where χ_f(G) denotes the fractional chromatic number. In particular, determine whether there are interesting such classes that are not χ-bounded, and whether χ-boundedness results can be extended to this broader setting.

evidence.quote: Which hereditary class C of graphs has a function f such that χ(G) ≤ f(χf(G)) for all graphs G ∈ C?
Are there some graph classes not χ-bounded but has such a function?

accepted.question_text: Fix integers m ≥ 2 and 0 ≤ ℓ < m. Determine whether one can find, in polynomial time, a shortest cycle in an input graph whose length is congruent to ℓ modulo m.

evidence.quote: Fix integers ℓ and m with 0 ≤ ℓ < m and m ⩾ 2. Can we find a shortest cycle of length ℓ mod m in the input graph G in polynomial time?

accepted.question_text: Let G_k(n) be the family of n-vertex graphs with no C_k-minor. Determine whether there exists a function f such that for every k there is a subgraph-universal host graph with no C_{f(k)}-minor and with n^{O_k(1)} vertices that contains every graph in G_k(n) as a subgraph.

evidence.quote: Let Gk(n) be the family of n-vertex graphs with no Ck-minor. Does there exists a function f such that for every k ⩾ 1 there exists a subgraph-universal graph with no C_{f(k)}-minor and n^{O_k(1)} vertices for Gk(n)?

accepted.question_text: Let d ≥ 0 and let G′ = G ⊠ K_{d+1}. Suppose the vertices of G′ can be partitioned into four sets V_1, …, V_4 such that each induced subgraph G′[V_i] has maximum degree at most d. Must the original graph G satisfy χ(G) ≤ 4?

evidence.quote: Question: Let G be a graph, d ⩾ 0 be an integer and let G′ = G ⊠ Kd+1. Suppose that there exists a partition V1, . . . , V4 of V (G′) such that ∆(G′|Vi) ≤ d for 1 ≤ i ≤ 4. Is it true that χ(G) ≤ 4?

accepted.question_text: Define a correct 2-dimensional analogue of graph tree decompositions for simplicial complexes. In particular, extend the notion of an H-decomposition from graphs to 2-dimensional simplicial complexes G and H in a way that interacts well with a suitable notion of bramble, so that large-hitting-number brambles remain the obstructions to low-overlap decompositions over contractible 2-complexes.

evidence.quote: Question: What is the “right” extension of this definition to 2-dimensional simplicial complexes G and H?
It would be nice to preserve this property, i.e. to have brambles with large hitting number to be (the only?) obstructions to decompositions over a contractible 2-complex with small overlap.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the centered chromatic number of a graph is always bounded linearly by its linear chromatic number. Concretely, decide whether χ_cen(G) ∈ O(χ_lin(G)) for all graphs G; the cited conjecture asks whether χ_cen(G) ≤ 2·χ_lin(G).

evidence.quote: Is it true that χcen(G) ∈ O(χlin(G))? Czerwiński-Nadara-Pilipczuk bravely conjecture that χcen(G) ≤ 2 χlin(G).

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the following guest classes have the Erdős–Pósa property in the stated host classes: geodesic cycles in all graphs; induced cycles of length congruent to 0 modulo 3 in all graphs; and pairs of linked cycles in graphs embedded in 3-space.
accepted.context_brief: Erdős–Pósa questions for special cycle classes

evidence.quote: 1. Do geodesic cycles have the Erdős-Pósa property in the class of all graphs? 2. Do induced cycles of length 0 mod 3 have the Erdős-Pósa property in the class of all graphs? 3. Do pairs of linked cycles have the Erdős-Pósa property in the class of graphs embedded in 3-space?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a monotone graph class with unbounded chromatic number that is minimal with that property, meaning every proper monotone subclass has bounded chromatic number? By the discussion in the source, it suffices to understand this for triangle-free monotone classes if one seeks a positive example.
accepted.context_brief: Minimal monotone class of unbounded chromatic number

evidence.quote: Does there exist a monotone class G of graphs with unbounded chromatic number which is minimal with that property, that is, for every proper monotone subclass H of G, the graphs in H have bounded chromatic number?
By Rödl’s result, it suffices to focus on classes of graphs G that are triangle-free.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a graph with a degree list assignment L, meaning |L(v)| = deg(v) for every vertex v. Characterize those graphs for which every such degree list assignment admits a fractional L-packing. The source also asks a related extension problem for 2-connected graphs in which any precolouring of a single vertex should extend under every degree list assignment, and asks the analogous two questions for correspondence colouring (DP-colouring).

evidence.quote: The question is: if G has a fractional L-packing no matter the degree list assignment L, what does G look like?

A helpful, related question: suppose G is a 2-connected graph. Suppose I can precolour any single vertex in G any way I like no matter the degree list assignment L, and always have that precolouring extend to a colouring of G. What does G look like?
We could also ask the same two questions for correspondence colouring (DP-colouring).

accepted.question_text: Find additional minimal 4-critical t-perfect graphs, ideally an infinite family, and determine whether every t-perfect graph is 4-colourable. The source notes that only two minimal 4-critical t-perfect examples are currently known and both are small.

evidence.quote: It is open whether they are 4-colorable. There are only two known minimal examples of 4-critical t-perfect graphs ... and they are both small graphs. This seems silly, and we would like more (ideally an infinite list of them).
